items.summary: Sources say former Google chief Eric Schmidt holds a 1% stake in Anthropic from an early investment. With the company's IPO approaching, his share could yield a massive windfall, potentially boosting his net worth to nearly $80 billion if valuations reach $2 trillion. Schmidt declined comment, as did Anthropic.
items.title: Eric Schmidt's Anthropic Stake Set for Huge Windfall

items.summary: China announced optimized export control measures for specific drone-related items, effective November 18, 2026. The Ministry of Commerce, General Administration of Customs, and the Equipment Development Department of the Central Military Commission jointly issued the rules. Items such as autopilots and certain unmanned aircraft require licenses. A spokesperson stated the move safeguards national security, fulfills international obligations, and maintains global supply chain stability.
items.title: China Optimizes Export Controls on Drone-Related Items

items.summary: Apple confirmed a product launch event titled 'Pro and tell' scheduled for October 28 in Los Angeles. The event is expected to feature a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen OLED display, marking a significant shift for the company. Additionally, Apple may introduce an M6 chip and an OLED iPad mini. Details remain largely unconfirmed beyond these expectations.
items.title: Apple Confirms 'Pro and Tell' Event Featuring Touchscreen Macs

items.summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt holds a 1% stake in Anthropic, reportedly worth $15–20 billion if the company's IPO proceeds as expected. Bloomberg cites sources familiar with the matter regarding the valuation. Schmidt invested in the startup's 2021 Series A round before Google entered. However, it remains unclear if he has sold any part of his holding since then.
items.title: Eric Schmidt's Anthropic Stake Could Yield Billions

items.summary: Pop superstar Dua Lipa is challenging Samsung in a US federal court, seeking at least $15 million in damages over the alleged unauthorized use of her photograph on television packaging. Lipa's legal team argues that Samsung used an image taken at the 2024 Austin City Limits music festival in a way that could mislead consumers into believing she endorsed the televisions. Samsung has rejected the allegations, stating the photograph was supplied by a third-party content partner and used after assurances that necessary permissions were obtained. The dispute centers on whether the image's placement implies official endorsement and involves questions of copyright, trademark, and publicity rights.
items.title: Dua Lipa Sues Samsung Over Unauthorized Use of Her Image on TV Boxes

items.summary: Researchers at the University of Technology Sydney developed an AI model using transformer technology to identify genetic risk factors for ischaemic stroke. The model identified 18 genetic variants and tested on over 40,000 people, showing high-risk individuals were 21% more likely to suffer a stroke. This tool aims to improve personalised prevention, complementing existing methods that account for roughly 38% of stroke risk through genetics.
items.title: UTS Researchers Develop AI Tool to Predict Stroke Risk from DNA

items.summary: Samsung is rolling out an Android 17 update with One UI 9.0 to the Galaxy A37, introducing new privacy features and interface changes. While the update has begun internationally, users are advised to consider potential impacts on daily use. The article also notes a future possibility that Samsung may rename One UI to Galaxy OS in 2027 with an Android 18-based update.
items.title: Samsung Galaxy A37 Receives Android 17 Update with New Privacy Features

items.summary: The US Homeland Security Department ordered the removal of DeepSeek products and services using the Chinese AI model from civilian agency IT systems. DHS cited multiple threat vectors and risks of data transfer to the PRC. The department also banned the acquisition of such products. Several agencies and states have previously imposed similar restrictions.
items.title: US Homeland Security Department Orders Removal of DeepSeek from Civilian Government Systems

items.summary: The Ministry of Commerce announced that China will impose export controls on tunnel boring machines and optimize measures for dredger-related items, effective November 18, 2026. A spokesperson stated these actions safeguard national security and align with international practices, noting the items' dual-use nature. China remains willing to engage in dialogue to maintain global supply chain stability.
items.title: China Imposes Export Controls on Tunnel Boring Machines

items.summary: Anthropic and Nscale are reportedly in talks for another $45 billion compute deal, according to Bloomberg citing sources. This potential agreement would follow a similar deal announced a month ago. While details remain uncertain, both companies are pursuing IPOs, with Nscale facing investor pushback over its $30 billion valuation.
items.title: Anthropic and Nscale Reportedly Discussing Another $45 Billion Compute Deal

items.summary: The Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC) has launched its AI Factory Accelerator Programme, offering startups sovereign compute, technical support, and training. This initiative complements the NVIDIA Inception program, which provides additional resources like mentoring and venture connections. Since its April 2025 launch, the BSC AI Factory has delivered over 800 services to clients, supporting innovations in sectors ranging from water management to healthcare.
items.title: Barcelona Supercomputing Center Launches AI Factory Accelerator for Startups

items.summary: OpenAI is accelerating its fundraising efforts to secure investor commitments before rival Anthropic's expected public market debut in mid-November. Sources indicate OpenAI aims to capitalize on recent revenue growth and reach a valuation over $1.4 trillion. The rapid timetable reflects competition for capital as both companies pursue trillion-dollar valuations. OpenAI is seeking to complete the round before Anthropic's financial disclosures invite comparisons. Investors face challenges evaluating two complex offerings amid market volatility and rising interest rates. Some companies have paused listings due to these concerns.
items.title: OpenAI Races to Secure Funding Before Anthropic IPO

items.summary: A podcast episode claims that flying, flipping, and fully self-driving electric vehicles are finally available for immediate purchase from Tesla's competitors. The host notes that while Tesla Roadster buyers still face uncertainty, other electric trucks with similar capabilities can be ordered today. The segment also promotes a solar installer service, EnergySage, which offers pre-vetted installers and potential savings of 20-30%.
items.title: Podcast Hosts Claim Flying Electric Vehicles Are Available Now

items.summary: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev met with visiting Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Sofia on October 19, 2026. Radev expressed willingness to elevate bilateral relations and expand cooperation, stating Bulgaria cherishes traditional friendship and views China as a stabilizing force. Wang agreed to deepen political trust and practical cooperation, noting China is ready to support Bulgaria's role in Eurasian connectivity.
items.title: Bulgarian PM and Chinese FM vow to expand bilateral cooperation

items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged businesses to embrace artificial intelligence at a summit in Berlin, highlighting an expected partnership with Nvidia to modernize Germany's industry. Merz emphasized AI's role in economic revival amidst global competition. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang noted existing collaborations with German carmakers and announced planned investments in local startups, while a government memorandum of understanding was signed.
items.title: German Chancellor Merz Urges AI Investment Amid Nvidia Partnership

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is arriving in India for high-level bilateral engagements focused on trade, investment, and energy cooperation. His itinerary includes talks in Mumbai with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and a visit to Jamnagar, home to Reliance Industries' oil refining complex. The visit occurs as the US faces rising domestic energy pressures, with diesel prices exceeding six dollars per gallon threatening to accelerate inflation ahead of midterm elections.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio Visits India for Trade and Energy Talks Amid Rising Diesel Prices

items.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has urged the country to prepare for the possibility of losing preferential access to the United States market under the African Growth and Opportunity Act. He warned the consequences would be devastating, though he cautioned citizens not to panic. The automotive industry faces high stakes, with estimates indicating around 86-thousand jobs at car manufacturers are directly linked to the agreement, rising to 125-thousand when subcontractors are included. The extension of the programme awaits President Donald Trump's signature.
items.title: Ramaphosa Warns South Africa of Devastating Impact from Potential US Trade Deal Loss

items.summary: At the Data + AI Summit 2026, Luis Alonso of HP detailed the company's strategy to build an AI-ready go-to-market data foundation using Databricks. HP unified customer data and third-party signals into a Marketing Lakehouse, deploying Genie and CustomerLake to provide trusted context for marketers. This approach reduced data sharing requests from three months to 48 hours. HP expanded intent-data ingestion from 75 to approximately 20,000 topics and created a media metric view with 26 dimensions and 10 measures. Alonso noted that while prior CDP setups might have taken two or three months, the new CustomerLake enabled audience readiness in two hours, with potential CDP total cost of ownership reductions of up to 40%. The strategy aims to bring identity signals back into the Databricks environment to support both B2C and B2B data models.
items.title: HP Builds AI-Ready Data Foundation with Databricks CustomerLake

items.summary: Tens of thousands of organizations rely on dbt for data transformation, but running it on Databricks can significantly reduce costs and improve speed. The article highlights practices such as using incremental strategies, materialized views, and Predictive Optimization to minimize unnecessary compute. Features like Liquid Clustering and Query tags further enhance efficiency and cost attribution. By adopting these platform-native capabilities, teams can streamline operations, reduce manual tuning, and achieve faster query performance while maintaining clear lineage and governance within their dbt projects.
items.title: How to Optimize dbt Workloads on Databricks for Cost and Speed

items.summary: Analysts suggest the EU may finally be ready to address trade issues with China. European capitals, having secured limits on hybrid vehicle imports, are developing tools to counter Beijing's trade surplus, according to an economist in The Wire China. However, a Chatham House expert notes that possessing trade instruments is insufficient without the capacity to utilize them. Former UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak has called for a coalition of nations to counter what he describes as a 'Chinese juggernaut,' warning of potential global dependency on China.
items.title: EU Seeks to Strengthen Trade Position Against China Amid Analyst Debate

items.summary: Nvidia-backed Nscale is in talks with Anthropic for a new AI cloud deal potentially worth US$45 billion, a source said on Oct 19. The deal involves a second facility at Nscale's Monarch campus in West Virginia, which would deliver 460 megawatts using Nvidia chips. Anthropic has already committed to spending US$45 billion for power from the first campus. Discussions regarding a third building are ongoing, with details subject to change.
items.title: Nscale and Anthropic Discuss Potential $45 Billion AI Cloud Deal

items.summary: China's GDP expanded by 4.5% year on year in the third quarter, an increase from 4.3% recorded in the second quarter. Officials attribute this acceleration to robust new growth drivers and fresh policy support, suggesting the economy remains on track to meet its full-year growth target. Additional data is available through accompanying charts.
items.title: China's Economy Shows Growth in Third Quarter

items.summary: US prosecutors allege that Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer, installed a covert recording device at the company's San Francisco office. Prosecutors claim Alfozan had support from the Saudi government, citing messages where a royal family member recruited him. Alfozan is charged with intercepting oral communications and faces potential additional charges. His lawyer argues the trip was for family reasons.
items.title: US Prosecutors Accuse Former OpenAI Engineer of Bugging Office with Alleged Saudi Support

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is reportedly tightening scrutiny of large overseas investments by domestic companies to contain capital outflows as the rupee tumbles more than 5% this year. The central bank issued a standardized checklist requiring banks to assess investment details, though it has not imposed new restrictions on such investments.
items.title: RBI Tightens Overseas Investment Scrutiny Amid Rupee Pressure

items.summary: US President Donald Trump thanked Elon Musk for pledging SpaceX shares to millions of American children through the Trump Accounts initiative. Musk plans to donate one share per child next year, an act described as the first of many. Bloomberg reported the agreement, noting that the specific distribution structure remains undisclosed. Estimates suggest the donation could be worth between $10.5 billion and $10.7 billion based on the number of eligible children and current share prices. The Trump Accounts program, established by a tax bill signed by Trump, provides tax-advantaged investment accounts for children under 18, aiming to give them a stake in the country's enterprise.
items.title: Trump thanks Musk for pledging SpaceX shares to children via Trump Accounts

items.summary: The Indian government is considering a hardware-based security system to monitor and control satellite internet traffic from foreign providers, including Elon Musk's Starlink. This proposal, currently under discussion according to a report in The Economic Times, involves routing communications through a government-controlled system to protect national security. Public sector research units and some private companies may participate in developing this measure.
items.title: India Considers Security System for Foreign Satellite Internet Providers

items.summary: The Indian Youth Congress burned an effigy of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, demanding his resignation over alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision of rolls. During the protest, titled 'Vote Chori Ki Raasleela,' IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib stated the group would continue actions until Kumar resigned or was jailed. The organization launched a digital campaign to identify what it calls the '10 heads of India's Ravan' and plans a virtual effigy burning. Opposition parties have also raised concerns regarding the electoral roll revision process.
items.title: Youth Congress Burns Ravan Effigy With CEC Gyanesh Kumar's Face

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is beginning a three-day visit to India to discuss a proposed bilateral trade deal, energy security, and strategic cooperation with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar. The agenda includes meetings in Mumbai and a tour of Reliance Industries' Jamnagar refinery. Negotiations on the trade pact, which has been ongoing since early 2025, are described as nearing a final stage despite friction over tariffs and immigration. Rubio, speaking ahead of the trip, stated the two sides are very close to finalizing the agreement. The visit also addresses strains in bilateral relations caused by US tariffs and disagreements over regional conflicts.
items.title: Rubio Visits India for Trade Deal and Energy Security Talks

items.summary: Jio Platforms' initial public offering opens on October 21, priced between Rs 1,065 and Rs 1,119 per share. The grey market premium indicates an indicative listing price of Rs 1,364 at the upper end. Mukesh Ambani-led Jio Platforms raised nearly Rs 8,110 crore from 212 anchor investors ahead of its Rs 30,213 crore issue. Brokerage Emkay recommends subscription, citing Jio's leading telecom position and growth potential in digital services. The company plans to use Rs 27,500 crore of proceeds to repay borrowings. Analysts project a post-issue market capitalisation of Rs 10.30 lakh crore.
items.title: Jio Platforms IPO Opens with Strong Grey Market Premium and Anchor Interest

items.summary: Korea's KOSPI index fell further as AI-related stocks continued a sharp decline. Chipmaker SK Hynix and data-center firm Elice Inc. saw significant drops, with Elice plunging up to 32% on its debut. Major bellwethers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics fell 35% and 22% respectively, contributing to the index trading about 39% below its peak. The sell-off follows a global reduction in AI-linked stock value exceeding $1 trillion. Investors are increasingly concerned about credit risks associated with heavy AI spending and rising capital costs, prompting calls to diversify beyond the sector as earnings growth projections moderate.
items.title: Korea's AI Stocks Plunge Amid Global Sell-Off and Valuation Concerns

items.summary: Gary Black of The Future Fund predicts SpaceX will buy Tesla at $420 per share in the coming weeks. He stated that an announcement could occur before Tesla's annual general meeting. Analysts at Barclays also suggested a merger might be announced soon. Walter Isaacson noted similarities between the companies, suggesting a future combination. The article discusses these rumors without confirming them.
items.title: Investor Predicts SpaceX Will Acquire Tesla At $420 Per Share

items.summary: The India-New Zealand free trade agreement entered into force, eliminating tariffs on 100% of Indian exports. New Zealand pledged $20 billion in investment over 15 years. Both nations aim to double bilateral trade to NZ$7 billion by 2030. The pact covers market access, investment, and talent mobility, with wine tariffs set to fall over a decade.
items.title: India and New Zealand Activate Free Trade Agreement

items.summary: Gideon Bornstein and Sasha Indarte find that expanding Medicaid increases credit card borrowing by 0.38% for every 1% rise in eligible population. They attribute this to improved financial resilience driving credit supply, contributing 30% of net welfare gains.
items.title: Expanded Medicaid Increases Credit Card Borrowing via Improved Financial Resilience

items.summary: Cerreia-Vioglio, Corrao, Flynn, and Lanzani characterize equilibria in economies with endogenous production networks, showing log-prices equal a min-max over networks of a primitive affine function of log-productivities. They generalize Hulten's theorem and find that smooth changes in Domar weights overstate adverse GDP effects by omitting option value.
items.title: Authors Characterize Equilibria in Economies with Endogenous Production Networks

items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government announced an additional 25 days of wage employment under the VB-G RAM G scheme for eligible rural households, bringing total support to 150 days annually. Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay directed authorities to prioritize vulnerable groups, including women and Scheduled Castes. A financial sanction of Rs 100 crore from the 2026-2027 budget supports this initiative, excluding Chennai from disbursement.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Govt Extends Wage Employment Support Under New Scheme

items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addressed the organization's 101st Foundation Day gathering in Nagpur, warning that global powers seek India's development but fear its power might challenge their dominance. He stated that regime-change agitations rarely resolve fundamental problems and often fuel social divisions rather than delivering solutions. Bhagwat cautioned that protests driven by political interests could become instruments of hostility, urging citizens to respect constitutional limits and civil discourse. He highlighted the need for discernment among the youth regarding information consumption and artificial intelligence, advocating for a Hindu vision rooted in universal brotherhood and balanced development over materialism.
items.title: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Warns Against Regime Change Agitations and Calls for Balanced Development

items.summary: Euro-area inflation reached 3.8% in September, the highest in recent months, driving protests across Europe over soaring energy and housing costs. While national governments control prices and rents, the EU coordinates oil stock releases and urges targeted aid after spending €17.9 billion cushioning bills this year. Spain's Prime Minister called a snap election following housing decree rejections.
items.title: Rising Inflation Sparks Protests Across Europe as EU Seeks Aid Role

items.summary: A German research team investigated using compressive stress relaxation measurement to monitor polymer degradation in aging photovoltaic modules. They fabricated mini-modules and subjected them to damp heat and combined heat and ultraviolet irradiation. The study found that encapsulant and backsheet degradation affected mechanical response and power degradation, suggesting that overacceleration in testing should be avoided for realistic reliability predictions. The findings were published in Polymer Testing.
items.title: German Researchers Use Non-Destructive Testing to Monitor PV Module Degradation

items.summary: A viral video shows Gufran Shaikh slapping a girl during a garba event in Nala Sopara, Maharashtra. Molestation allegations against him prompted protests by Hindu organisations. The incident occurred on Monday, raising concerns over girls' safety at such events. Authorities face demands for strict legal action against those accused in the case.
items.title: Man Accused of Molestation Slaps Girl at Garba Event Sparking Protests

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey has dismissed calls from Labour MPs to increase Capital Gains Tax ahead of the Budget. While some ministers previously supported raising the tax, Healey is minded not to do so, citing warnings that it could cost the government money if wealthy people leave the country or defer selling assets. Healey aims to foster wealth creation and confidence in British business.
items.title: Chancellor Rejects Calls to Raise Capital Gains Tax

items.summary: NAB announced the axing of 2,500 staff as a calculated move to improve efficiency, though the article questions whether this trend among major corporations signals an impending recession. While NAB Chief Executive Andrew Irvine stated that customer-facing roles would not be materially impacted, the article highlights broader economic headwinds, including stagnant productivity growth of -0.2 per cent over 12 months and rising interest rates. Experts warn that if other major banks and corporations follow suit, the resulting job losses could trigger a negative feedback loop, potentially pushing unemployment to 5 per cent and causing a recession. The Reserve Bank has already hiked rates four times this year to combat inflation, with some economists predicting further hikes may be necessary.
items.title: NAB Job Cuts Spark Recession Fears Amid Economic Pressure

items.summary: JinkoSolar has unveiled a 510 W all-black residential solar panel featuring 25.5% efficiency and a 40-year warranty. The module utilizes TOPCon-based Amorphous-Si Passivating Cell technology to target premium applications like villas and homes with limited space. JinkoSolar CEO Charlie Cao stated the panel is tailored for premium rooftops, while the company has identified Europe and Australia as target markets. Commercial availability and pricing remain undisclosed.
items.title: JinkoSolar Unveils High-Efficiency 510 W Residential Solar Module

items.summary: UK job vacancies fell by 21,000 to 691,000 in the three months to September, the largest drop since the start of the year. The Office for National Statistics reports small firms scaled back hiring due to labour costs. Energy prices rose after the Iran war began, and increases in National Insurance and the minimum wage also made employing staff more expensive.
items.title: UK Job Vacancies Drop Sharply as Small Firms Cut Hiring

items.summary: France plans to equip Rafale fighters with a new Hammer XLR variant to address gaps in suppressing enemy air defenses. General Jérôme Bellanger highlighted the weapon's potential during testimony. The variant, expected to be operational by 2028, uses a miniature turbojet engine for extended range. This development is reported by Opex360 based on National Assembly testimony.
items.title: France Develops New Hammer Variant for Rafale Fighters

items.summary: UK unemployment fell to 4.7% in June to August, beating forecasts. The Office for National Statistics reports employment rose, but vacancies dropped by 21,000 to 691,000. Smaller firms cite increased labour costs as a key factor.
items.title: UK unemployment falls as firms cut vacancies

items.summary: Actor Romeo Tan reveals he owns five power banks, having previously owned up to eight. He states that his phone battery dropping to 70 per cent causes him anxiety. Tan explains his collection stems from a need for security and reassurance against unpredictable situations. He notes that his co-stars appreciate his ability to lend power sources. The article, originally published in 8Days, highlights his ongoing interest in buying new technology.
items.title: Actor Romeo Tan Admits to Power Bank Obsession

items.summary: UEFA sent a letter to FIFA requesting answers regarding Gianni Infantino's presidency, specifically concerning the FIFA Forward Enterprise project and the FIFA Peace Prize. UEFA General Secretary Theodore Theodoridis wrote to FIFA's Mattias Grafstrom seeking swift responses to 42 questions covering 12 topics. Infantino, who is up for reelection in March 2027, apologized to the FIFA Council and invited written questions for a December meeting. UEFA and FIFA did not immediately respond to comment requests.
items.title: UEFA Demands Answers from FIFA on Infantino Presidency

items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated at a Nagpur event that the Kolkata Durga Puja stampede, which killed 19 people, resulted from human error rather than nature. He attributed the tragedy to foreign attempts to destabilize India. Meanwhile, Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan claimed ongoing protests against the Chief Election Commissioner were a fight for regime change, prompting BJP leaders to label the demonstrations as fronts for overthrowing the government.
items.title: RSS Chief Bhagwat Blames Human Error for Kolkata Stampede

items.summary: The Australian Medical Association's Tasmanian branch has called for an independent inquiry into the state's health system, describing it as being in a 'perpetual crisis'. AMA president Meg Creely argues that piecemeal fixes have failed to address interconnected problems like emergency department blockages and ambulance ramping. This call follows a recent patient death and comes as the state government plans to cut $700 million from the health department. Health Minister Bridget Archer dismissed the proposal, citing a cost of upwards of $30 million and duplication of existing work. Despite these metrics, performance indicators such as elective surgery waitlists and ambulance response times continue to worsen.
items.title: Tasmanian Doctors Demand Health Inquiry Amid System Crisis

items.summary: Alberta voters rejected a proposal to begin a process toward independence in a referendum, with about 76% supporting remaining in Canada compared to 23% backing separation. Results showed a victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney and Canadian unity supporters. The vote was not a direct referendum on independence but would have set the province on a path toward a future vote on separation from Canada.
items.title: Alberta Voters Reject Independence Referendum in Support of Canadian Unity

items.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines lost a leg after being struck by a car in a suspected deliberate attack outside her Wangaratta office. Local media and the ABC reported the amputation following surgery. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated the incident appeared intentional, noting rising political violence. A 43-year-old man was arrested, and local barber Ricky Jeffries was hailed for restraining the driver until police arrived.
items.title: Australian MP Seriously Hurt in Suspected Car Attack

items.summary: The Gujarat government approved a 978-square-metre plot in Vadodara for former cricketer Yusuf Pathan, ending a 14-year stalemate. Valued at Rs 20.53 crore, the land is adjacent to his residence. While the state government issued orders to the Vadodara Municipal Corporation, the final price and payment terms remain pending. Pathan must wait for the VMC Standing Committee to clear the proposal before taking possession.
items.title: Gujarat Govt Approves Land Allotment to Yusuf Pathan After Decade-Long Delay

items.summary: Vinted sellers report unfair account bans and a lack of meaningful appeals. Catherine Warrilow and Victoria Chamberlain-Ralphs describe losing money and accounts after disputes, citing automated systems that act as judge and jury. Consumer expert Martyn James notes a flood of similar complaints regarding counterfeit allegations and frozen funds. While Vinted states all appeals are handled by human reviewers and 98% of transactions complete smoothly, sellers argue the process lacks transparency and independent review. The platform operates across 26 markets, generating significant revenue, yet faces criticism over its dispute resolution mechanisms.
items.title: Vinted sellers complain of unfair account bans and lack of appeal

items.summary: The article explores the controversy surrounding AI-generated actors, using a digital recreation of Val Kilmer as a catalyst for debate. While some industry figures like Adil Alimzhanov of Higgsfield AI argue that the technology is liberating and capable of capturing internal states, others like Tim Webber and Zack London remain skeptical about AI's ability to replicate genuine human emotion and complexity. The piece highlights the tension between fully synthetic performances and hybrid approaches that retain a human core, questioning whether AI can ever truly rival the authenticity of flesh-and-blood performers.
items.title: AI Film Stars Face Skepticism Amidst Rapid Technological Advancement

items.summary: An unverified document attributed to India's Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) suggests stricter labelling requirements for herbal supplements. The text, dated October 15, lists 16 botanical entries with specific dosage ranges and warnings, such as restrictions on Neem leaf powder for those planning to conceive. However, the document's authenticity could not be independently confirmed, as it does not appear in FSSAI's official archive. Consequently, the contents are treated as provisional pending verification. If authenticated, the advisory would mandate immediate compliance with existing regulations regarding formulations and packaging.
items.title: Unverified FSSAI Advisory Proposes Stricter Herbal Supplement Labelling

items.summary: A Kenyan court found Paul Mackenzie and 28 associates guilty of murdering 191 people, including 190 children, in the Shakahola starvation cult massacre. The verdict followed the 2023 discovery of hundreds of bodies. Francis Wanje, who lost eight family members, welcomed the ruling after years of waiting. Sentencing is expected on November 6.
items.title: Kenya Court Convicts Preacher and Associates in Shakahola Massacre

items.summary: CBC projects that Alberta voters overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin a process toward independence. With over 1 million votes counted, approximately 76% supported remaining in Canada versus 23% backing separation. While the vote was not explicitly about independence, it exposed political divisions and raised questions about national unity. Delays at roughly 100 of 1,400 polling stations pushed results back by more than two hours. Prime Minister Mark Carney and Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre urged unity, while separatists vowed to continue their push. The Alberta premier, Danielle Smith, plans to vote to remain but will not require her party members to do so.
items.title: Alberta Voters Reject Independence Referendum Plan

items.summary: A Meiji Yasuda Life survey found only 28.2% of Japanese parents want a second child, citing financial pressures. Economist Kazutaka Maeda noted a 57% drop since 2020, attributing it to rising costs rather than waning desire.
items.title: Survey Reveals Few Japanese Parents Want Second Child Due to Costs

items.summary: Andy Burnham has launched a campaign against 'loudcasting' on public transport, urging passengers to use headphones and proposing new guidance for local authorities to impose fines of up to £100 for nuisance behaviour. While train operating companies already have powers to fine up to £1,000 for antisocial behaviour, enforcement remains unclear, with bus drivers noting a lack of capacity to police passengers. Recent polling suggests about 88% of Britons consider playing music out loud unacceptable. Critics argue the policy may be a distraction from more serious issues like escalating abuse on transport, while others see it as a necessary step to address growing anxiety about social cohesion. The article explores whether gentle nudges or stricter enforcement will effectively alter public behaviour.
items.title: Andy Burnham launches campaign against loudcasting on public transport

items.summary: The Indian government is developing a central scheme to incentivize states on agrivoltaics, which involves installing solar panels above existing farmland. Ministry of New and Renewable Energy secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi stated the initiative aims to boost solar capacity, though it remains undecided whether it will be a standalone program or part of the PM Kusum 2.0 scheme. The government noted that such installations are currently 25% more expensive than conventional ground-mounted panels, but the scheme intends to cover these costs to ensure commercial viability. Initial assessments suggest a potential for 1-2 Terawatts of installation across the country. This development coincides with the upcoming 7th Agrivoltaics World Conference in Delhi.
items.title: Govt Plans Central Agrivoltaics Scheme Ahead of Conference

items.summary: Alberta voters are set to reject separation from Canada, a result projected by the Canadian Broadcasting Corp. after approximately 1 million votes were counted, with roughly 76% favoring remaining in the country. This outcome supports Prime Minister Mark Carney following a divisive campaign. The decision aims to alleviate business fears regarding uncertainty during an anticipated energy boom.
items.title: Alberta Voters Reject Separation as Carney Wins Referendum

items.summary: On October 2, 2026, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stated on national television that there are no instructions to hold back or limit the use of all weapons available to domestic security forces. The article describes a wave of state violence against schoolchildren in France during the autumn of 2026, involving ultra-militarised police and riot squads deploying high-velocity weapons like stun grenades and flashball launchers. This crackdown coincides with a youth uprising against poor school conditions and the upcoming presidential election, where radical left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon is a frontrunner against Marine Le Pen. The government has faced criticism for its response, including a ban on stun grenades that was later lifted after a child suffered a hand injury from a grenade in Saint-Étienne on October 17.
items.title: French Interior Minister Defends Police Use of Weapons Against Schoolchildren

items.summary: China's blue-chip CSI300 Index dropped 0.5% by the lunch break, while the Shanghai Composite Index was 0.1% weaker. The CSI Banks Index and financial sector were both down 1.4%, dragging the broader market lower. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng was down 1%, and the Hang Seng Tech Index slid 1.2% to a two-year low. Policymakers left benchmark lending rates unchanged for the 17th straight month in October, signaling no rush for further easing following strong GDP readings.
items.title: China and Hong Kong shares weaken as stable growth eases stimulus bets

items.summary: BBC Verify analyzed President Donald Trump's claims regarding the US economy ahead of midterm elections. While the US economy is growing at 2.2% annually, inflation has risen to 3.7% due to tariffs and the US-Israel war. Household incomes are rising, yet the middle and poorest fifths are estimated to be worse off by $1,700 and $750 respectively in 2026 compared to a no-tariff scenario. Job creation has slowed to 34,000 monthly from 122,000 under Biden, and borrowing costs have increased, with the 10-year bond yield above 5%. Trump stated, 'We have the hottest country anywhere in the world.'
items.title: BBC Verify examines US economic claims under Trump

items.summary: Guardian columnist Gaby Hinsliff argues that artificial intelligence risks creating bottlenecks in public services rather than saving time. Drawing parallels to the email crisis, she notes that while AI tools were intended to streamline state machinery, they are instead generating surges in complaints and requests. Hinsliff cites reports of a 39% rise in employment tribunal cases in England, Scotland, and Wales, partly due to claimants using AI to draft claims. She warns that as more people adopt agentic AI, the resulting flood of automated interactions could overwhelm human staff, turning shortcuts into systemic paralysis. The article suggests that time saved in one area often reappears elsewhere, necessitating new frictions to manage the impact.
items.title: Columnist Warns AI May Create Public Service Bottlenecks

items.summary: Paras Healthcare has secured Rs 652.5 crore from 39 anchor investors, including SBI Mutual Fund and BlackRock, for its upcoming IPO. The company plans to utilize the proceeds to repay debt. The IPO is scheduled to open on October 21 and conclude on October 23, with shares expected to list on October 28. The firm operates eight hospitals across five states and one Union Territory.
items.title: Paras Healthcare Secures Anchor Funding Ahead of IPO Launch

items.summary: Brent crude prices rose above $110 per barrel as traders grew pessimistic about oil flows from the Persian Gulf following reports of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler noted export rates have declined significantly, while ING analysts stated the market is pricing in a significant risk premium due to ongoing Middle East tensions.
items.title: Brent Crude Tops $110 Amid Tanker Attacks in Persian Gulf

items.summary: A new NBER working paper argues that evaluating immigration requires modeling labor-market and fiscal channels jointly. Using a general-equilibrium model calibrated to 17 OECD countries from 2015 to 2019, the authors find that native welfare often rises when inflows match recent skill compositions. The study suggests gains from trade can overwhelm apparent net fiscal costs, challenging views that focus on single channels.
items.title: Study Combines Labor and Fiscal Channels to Assess Immigration Impact

items.summary: The Allahabad High Court stayed the murder conviction and life sentence of Nandan Lal Rai, who seeks to contest Uttar Pradesh elections. Citing the right to livelihood, the court granted bail pending appeal, noting that losing the chance to run for office could result from a denied stay. Rai, associated with Mukhtar Ansari, was convicted in 2025 for a 2017 murder.
items.title: Allahabad High Court Stays Murder Conviction for UP Election Candidate

items.summary: Reliance Jio Infocomm is seeking a valuation of approximately ₹10 lakh crore, positioning itself as a technology platform spanning 5G, cloud, and AI rather than just a telecom operator. The company cites its role in carrying about 60% of India's wireless data traffic and its massive customer base as evidence of scale. Financial data shows revenue rising to ₹1,46,885.8 crore in fiscal 2026, with EBITDA increasing 16.4% to ₹73,382.1 crore. Proceeds from the offering will largely repay borrowings. Analysts note that while Jio has built a vast audience through low prices, the IPO tests its ability to convert this into higher earnings through new services.
items.title: Jio Seeks ₹10 Lakh Crore Valuation as Tech Platform

items.summary: AstraZeneca announced a partnership with Oracle to utilize AI and real-world data for patient identification and safety monitoring in clinical trials. The collaboration targets areas like cancer and cardiovascular diseases, aiming to address recruitment challenges and improve research efficiency as the company seeks to expand its medicine portfolio.
items.title: AstraZeneca Partners with Oracle on AI-Driven Clinical Trials

items.summary: China stated it will safeguard its firms' rights following US instructions to remove DeepSeek products. Foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning condemned the move as an over-generalization of national security concerns and the politicization of technology.
items.title: China Vows to Protect Firms After US AI Ban

items.summary: A shipment of Nvidia RTX 5090 graphics cards valued at ₹4.45 crore vanished from Guarulhos International Airport in Brazil. Distributor Oderço, which has operated for 38 years, reported the incident as its first such occurrence. The cause remains unknown, with no official explanation provided yet.
items.title: Nvidia RTX 5090 Shipment Vanishes at Brazil Airport

items.summary: A review of Google's new premium laptops, the Googlebook, notes that while the hardware meets high standards with features like backlit keyboards and fast chips, the software experience is currently underdeveloped. The devices run a hybrid of ChromeOS and Android, allowing for quick setup and deep phone integration. However, the reviewer found that most Android apps are poorly optimized for desktop use, and features like file syncing and the Gemini AI integration are unreliable. Despite the impressive build quality of models from Acer and Asus, the reviewer concludes that the software limitations make the £1,000 price point difficult to justify at this stage.
items.title: Review finds Google's new premium laptops have excellent hardware but flawed software

items.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh warned against double standards in fighting terrorism during an SCO meeting in Dushanbe, with Pakistan's deputy PM present. He stated that terrorism disrupts commerce and radicalises society. Singh noted that since 2014, the 'shelf life' of most terrorists has fallen to less than a year. He emphasized India's commitment to peace while remaining prepared to confront security challenges.
items.title: Rajnath Singh warns against terrorism double standards at SCO meeting

items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat linked Captain Smit Machchhar's actions on a Flydubai flight to Hindu values during a Vijayadashami speech. Bhagwat stated that these traditions inspire individuals to protect lives and ensure safety. The captain fought off an attacking co-pilot on a flight carrying 174 people, sustaining wounds while passengers intervened. Bhagwat emphasized that such innate courage strengthens national unity and reflects the inclusive nature of Hindu society.
items.title: RSS Chief Bhagwat Links Captain Machchhar's Heroism to Hindu Values

items.summary: Jio Platforms is launching a Rs 30,213-crore public offering, potentially becoming India's largest IPO. Analysts compare its valuation against Bharti Airtel, noting Jio's P/E multiple of 33.3 times at the upper price band is lower than Airtel's 40.71 times. While Jio offers scale and digital growth potential, Airtel commands higher ARPU and returns. Experts suggest the choice depends on whether investors prioritize Jio's growth trajectory or Airtel's established profitability and lower valuation risk.
items.title: Analysts Compare Jio IPO Valuation Against Bharti Airtel Shares

items.summary: Scientists have identified a new seahorse species, Hippocampus amandavincentae, from the Indian Ocean, resolving over a century of taxonomic confusion regarding the thorny seahorse. Based on two specimens collected from trawler bycatch in Tamil Nadu, the study reveals that what was once thought to be a single species is actually three distinct ones. Lead author Shalu Kannan noted that the discovery highlights the importance of identification for conservation. The new species, named after Project Seahorse co-founder Amanda Vincent, is thought to be endemic to the Indian Ocean, though its full range and conservation status require further investigation due to threats from illegal trade and fishing.
items.title: Scientists Identify New Seahorse Species in Indian Ocean

items.summary: Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary criticized European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen as 'useless' and called for taxes on US and Chinese airlines. He announced Ryanair is cutting a million seats from Belgium due to rising air travel taxes. O'Leary warned of significant fare rises in 2027 driven by higher oil prices, noting Brent crude topped $110 per barrel.
items.title: Ryanair CEO Criticizes EU Chief Over Aviation Taxes and Fare Hikes

items.summary: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu announced new curfews for Tuesday in areas requiring them, stating previous measures helped maintain calm. France recently experienced severe rioting six months before the presidential election. While some curfews were temporary, others in cities like Bordeaux and Nice extended for several days. Lyon saw demonstrations despite bans, with organizers gathering to support shopkeepers affected by looting. The government pledged support for businesses, though the Medef lobby accused the state of failing during the unrest.
items.title: French PM Announces New Curfews Amid Widespread Urban Unrest

items.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addressed protesters during his annual Vijayadashami speech in Nagpur, stating that while agitation is a democratic right, it must aim for solutions rather than deepening social divisions. He warned that movements driven by political objectives or external forces could fuel hostility and weaken the country. Bhagwat emphasized that problems are not solved through agitation alone but require collective action and dialogue. He cited improvements in 1,296 schools across 210 districts in 21 states as an example of societal effort. Bhagwat called on all sides, including protesters, the government, and political leaders, to ensure actions remain within constitutional limits and do not create discord.
items.title: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Urges Protesters to Focus on Solutions Over Division

items.summary: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, who is set to superannuate this month, flew a Kiran aircraft at the Air Force Academy in Dundigal near Hyderabad on Tuesday. This sortie occurred after his final fighter jet flight aboard an indigenous Tejas on October 12 during Exercise Tarang Shakti at Jodhpur Air Force Station. Singh passed out from the academy in 1984 with a Sword of Honour.
items.title: IAF Chief Flies Kiran Aircraft Near Hyderabad Before Retirement

items.summary: A civil society group in Manipur called for a 48-hour strike to protest the killing of three Meiteis by suspected militants. Markets, schools, and businesses closed in five districts, disrupting normal life. Security was tightened as the Native People Committee Manipur staged protests. The conflict, which began in May 2023, has claimed at least 306 lives.
items.title: Civil Society Group Calls 48-Hour Strike Over Meitei Killings in Manipur

items.summary: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu stated that authorities could announce further localized curfews if the situation requires it following weekend protests against high living costs. Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin reported 2,513 people taken into custody and 67 imprisoned. While partial curfews are in effect in Paris and Lyon, the government rejected a state of emergency, preferring firmness. Business federation Medef President Patrick Martin cited preliminary estimates that at least 3,000 businesses were affected by the unrest.
items.title: French Prime Minister Says Authorities May Impose More Curfews After Protest Violence

items.summary: An international dance production titled 'Subject to Change' will premiere in Luxembourg before staging at Sadler's Wells in London in autumn 2028 and visiting Tokyo in 2029. Spanish choreographer Marcos Morau created the show, featuring new choral arrangements of David Bowie's songs. Morau draws inspiration from Bowie's artistic reinventions, such as Ziggy Stardust and the Thin White Duke, aiming to transform individual songs into a collective experience. The production will incorporate global choral traditions and vocals from Spanish singer Maria Arnal, avoiding simple nostalgia to explore how Bowie's work transcends generations.
items.title: New Dance Production Honors David Bowie's Alter Egos

items.summary: Chancellor John Healey will not raise capital gains tax in next week's budget, despite calls from colleagues Louise Haigh and Wes Streeting. Treasury sources warn that increases might cost the Treasury if wealthy individuals defer asset sales. Instead, Healey plans to tax bank profits, with HSBC, NatWest, Barclays, and Lloyds generating £200bn in pre-tax profits over five years.
items.title: Chancellor Healey Rejects Capital Gains Tax Rise Amid Revenue Concerns

items.summary: The Yemeni army reported that 129 Houthi fighters were killed and 176 others wounded during clashes and airstrikes in Taiz province over the past 48 hours. Government forces, supported by local fighters, continued their offensive against Houthi positions in the al-Misrakh district and al-Aqrud front. Warplanes conducted 13 airstrikes targeting Houthi positions and equipment across the province. The Houthis have tightened their siege of Taiz city following recent government advances.
items.title: Yemeni Army Reports Heavy Houthi Losses in Taiz Offensive

items.summary: The Land and Environment Court heard an appeal by Nakar Property regarding a refused application for a 16-megawatt gas-fired power plant in the Southern Highlands. Community members argued that fragmented planning decisions overlook the cumulative impacts of multiple proposed plants. Concerns were raised about Aboriginal heritage, health risks, and water catchment safety, while the court considers evidence from the developer and council over the next three days.
items.title: Court hears appeal over data centre gas plants in Southern Highlands

items.summary: The Western Australian government has proposed new laws to prevent religious schools from discriminating against staff and students based on sexuality or disability. Attorney General Tony Buti stated the exemption will remain solely for religion. Felicity Creagh expressed relief, noting the laws offer greater protections for families with disabled children. The bill aims to be the largest overhaul of state anti-discrimination laws in over 40 years.
items.title: WA Government Proposes New Anti-Discrimination Laws for Religious Schools

items.summary: Laura Sartore, CEO of Ecoprogetti, argues that European solar module manufacturing should adopt a medium-scale model rather than replicating the massive gigafactories seen in India and the United States. Speaking at the NetZero Milan Expo Summit 2026, she stated that an ideal factory capacity for Europe ranges from 1 GW to 3 GW. Sartore explained that this scale balances economies of scale with financial viability, noting that facilities larger than 3 GW introduce excessive management costs and financial exposure. She emphasized that Europe's fragmented market and industrial structure, historically built on small and medium-sized enterprises, are better served by a network of medium-sized manufacturers capable of handling diverse project requirements.
items.title: Laura Sartore Advocates Medium-Scale Solar Factories in Europe

items.summary: Indian cricketing legends Sachin Tendulkar, Gautam Gambhir, VVS Laxman, and Suryakumar Yadav extended Dussehra greetings on Tuesday. They shared messages emphasizing hope, courage, and the triumph of good over evil. Tendulkar urged people to overcome inner battles, while Gambhir highlighted standing up for truth. Laxman wished for health and prosperity, and Suryakumar celebrated the victory of righteousness. The festival symbolizes this triumph across India.
items.title: Indian Cricket Legends Extend Dussehra Wishes with Messages of Hope and Courage

items.summary: A Japanese cybersecurity company stated that a Chinese-developed artificial intelligence tool named Artex was used to launch cyberattacks causing massive security breaches on Japanese companies. A specialist at GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae announced the detection of Artex based on forensic logs. The firm noted the attacks may be similar to those targeting South Korean financial organizations involving the same tool.
items.title: Japanese Cybersecurity Firm Identifies Chinese AI Tool in Attacks

items.summary: ABB has launched the UNIREC H2 rectifier to reduce energy losses in green hydrogen projects. The device achieves up to 99.6% efficiency and supports plants from megawatt-scale to over 1 GW. ABB states that improving power conversion efficiency is vital as electricity accounts for 60-70% of operating costs. Global demand for hydrogen exceeded 100 million tonnes in 2025, with installed capacity doubling to over 4 GW that year.
items.title: ABB Launches High-Efficiency Rectifier for Green Hydrogen Production

items.summary: A Mumbai Police team returned to Kota with three suspects apprehended in connection with the firing on Tiger Shroff's car. Although the team was expected to travel to Mumbai, they decided to stay back due to security concerns and fatigue. The suspects, including two adults and a minor, are now under tight security at a local police station while investigations continue.
items.title: Mumbai Police Return to Kota with Suspects Amid Security Concerns

items.summary: SSE has begun operations at its first Italian renewable electricity asset, a 17.3 MW wind farm in Puglia. The facility, comprising Castel Favorito and Masseria la Cattiva, exports energy to the local grid. This milestone supports a long-term agreement with Microsoft and marks a significant step in SSE's growth within Italy.
items.title: SSE Launches First Italian Wind Farm in Puglia

items.summary: Asian spot market LNG prices topped $30 per million British thermal units for the first time since December 2022, according to Bloomberg. This rise follows reports of an LNG tanker attack in the Red Sea. While Europe faces high prices and low storage levels, Asian demand may decline further as nations consider alternatives like coal.
items.title: Asian LNG Prices Surge Past $30 Amid Middle East Shipping Risks

items.summary: Italy allocated €770.4 million under the Agrisolare scheme for 7,409 projects totaling approximately 505 MW of rooftop solar capacity on agricultural buildings. The Gestore dei Servizi Energetici (GSE) published the list, noting that 1,863 eligible applications were not funded due to budget exhaustion. Agriculture Minister Francesco Lollobrigida stated the government hopes to find additional resources for remaining applicants.
items.title: Italy Allocates €770 Million for Agricultural Rooftop Solar

items.summary: New Agriculture Minister Arata Takebe addresses growing opposition from Hokkaido constituents regarding increased potato imports from the United States. Representing a district that supplies about 80% of Japan's domestically grown potatoes, Takebe stated on Oct. 15 that the government will take a firm stance in negotiations while acknowledging farmers' worries. He is the son of a former agriculture minister and a six-term Lower House member.
items.title: Japan's New Agriculture Minister Faces Domestic Opposition to US Potato Imports

items.summary: Japan's 20-year JGB yield fell as much as 6 basis points to 3.71%, its lowest level since September 9, following a record-strong auction outcome. The auction received bids worth 5.84 times the amount sold, the highest ratio since 1987. Takashi Fujiwara of Resona Asset Management noted that expectations of early interest rate hikes terminating by March next year are positive for the sector.
items.title: Japan's 20-year bond yield drops to lowest level since September

items.summary: Jamie Dimon, CEO of JPMorgan Chase, stated the bank will not permit external AI agents to access customer accounts or execute transactions due to significant security and liability risks. While the bank uses AI internally and supports secure data sharing, it currently blocks autonomous agents from acting on behalf of users. Dimon emphasized that customers authorizing such agents must understand the associated liability transfer.
items.title: JPMorgan CEO Rejects External AI Agents Over Security Risks

items.summary: A 20-year Japanese government bond auction attracted bids 5.84 times the offering volume, surpassing the previous month's 4.01 times ratio. This demand propelled the yen 0.2% higher to 158.15 against the US dollar. Analysts note the auction signals returning institutional cash and structural support for Japanese assets, while European sovereign risk pricing remains a factor for the euro.
items.title: Strong JGB Auction Demand Boosts Yen and Eases Euro Pressure

items.summary: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu stated that targeted curfews helped bring calm to French cities following weekend riots. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez admitted police lost control in some areas, leading to his rejected resignation. Over 2,500 people were arrested, and about 1,000 officers were injured. Further restrictions depend on local needs.
items.title: French PM Says Curfews Calmed Riots After Weekend Violence

items.summary: The US Department of Justice charged two Indian citizens, Amandeep Kaur and Kamlesh Shah, with election fraud in California. They were among 28 green card holders accused of unlawfully registering to vote and casting ballots in the 2024 presidential election. While 11 individuals were arrested, it remains unclear if Kaur and Shah were included. Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter urged verification of voter citizenship.
items.title: Two Indians Charged with Election Fraud in US

items.summary: Alberta has overwhelmingly rejected a plan to seek independence from Canada, with unofficial results showing nearly 77% support for remaining in the country. The nonbinding referendum, held outside Quebec, marks the first such vote in the province. Premier Danielle Smith, who opposed the vote, stated that Albertans voted for a stronger, united Canada.
items.title: Alberta Rejects Independence Bid in Referendum

items.summary: Mumbai Police took custody of three suspects arrested in Kota regarding the firing incident involving Tiger Shroff's car. A local court granted a 48-hour transit remand, allowing the Maharashtra Police team to transport the accused to Mumbai for further investigation. The suspects are expected to undergo detailed interrogation once they arrive in the city.
items.title: Mumbai Police Transport Three Suspects in Tiger Shroff Shooting Case

items.summary: Thomas Kurian of Google Cloud introduced Gemini for government services, a preview tool designed to automate complex public sector workflows. The agent connects securely to existing agency systems like Oracle and Salesforce without migrating data, adhering to strict data sovereignty and compliance requirements. It assists with tasks such as FOIA discovery, document redaction, and grant audits by grounding outputs in source documents. Tim Marczewski of the State of Missouri Office of Administration noted the tool aims to move government operations at the speed of modern life rather than traditional paperwork. The solution is built on Google Cloud's secure foundation and is available for federal, state, and local agencies.
items.title: Google Cloud Launches Gemini Agent for Government Services

items.summary: Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning criticized the US government for ordering agencies to stop using AI tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek. Mao stated that China opposes politicizing science and technology, asserting that the nation will resolutely safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies. The remarks were made during a regular news briefing on Tuesday.
items.title: China Criticizes US Ban on DeepSeek AI Tools

items.summary: Samsung is constructing a new semiconductor complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, to meet surging demand for memory chips driven by generative AI. Construction on a fifth facility, halted in 2024 due to low demand, has restarted. Samsung predicts memory demand will continue to surge through 2028. The project aims to reclaim market leadership against rival SK Hynix.
items.title: Samsung Rebuilds Pyeongtaek Chip Hub Amid AI Memory Surge

items.summary: OpenAI is accelerating its fundraising efforts ahead of rival Anthropic's expected November IPO, aiming to secure commitments from investors including SoftBank and MGX for a potential round of about US$30 billion. Sources indicate OpenAI seeks to capitalize on recent revenue growth from its GPT-6 Astra model, projecting annualised revenue to reach US$70 billion by the end of 2026. The push comes amid market volatility and concerns over AI valuations, with OpenAI currently valued at US$852 billion. Both companies face scrutiny as they compete for capital in a challenging market environment.
items.title: OpenAI Races to Raise Capital Before Anthropic IPO

items.summary: Nithin Kamath warned that pump-and-dump schemes via WhatsApp remain a risk in 2026, citing an ED investigation into a manipulation scheme involving two listed companies. The agency froze trading accounts holding shares worth around Rs 200 crore after searching 29 premises across six cities. Kamath urged investors to verify tips using AI tools before acting.
items.title: WhatsApp stock tips: Nithin Kamath warns of more pump-and-dump schemes as ED freezes accounts worth Rs 200 crore

items.summary: Singapore-based semiconductor firm Mi Material is raising $215 million through an initial public offering to fund expansion into the US and Malaysia. The company, a top-two global supplier of solder spheres, plans to invest $168.2 million of the proceeds in a US research and development centre. Chief executive Kevin Tan highlighted a 28% compound annual growth rate and stable gross margins, positioning the materials business as a defensive investment within the semiconductor sector. The firm aims to develop new thermal conducting layers to improve chip efficiency.
items.title: Mi Material Raises $215 Million in IPO to Expand Globally

items.summary: NVIDIA Helion and CompileIQ optimize PyTorch GPU kernels by searching compiler controls below the autotuner. Joint tuning of kernel configurations and PTXAS controls yields 4.7% speedups on optimized kernels, validated statistically.
items.title: NVIDIA Helion and CompileIQ Optimize PyTorch Kernels via Compiler Controls

items.summary: Microsoft has withdrawn from a data center deal with British provider Nscale in Loughton, Essex, reportedly due to electricity supply delays extending into the 2030s. Reuters cited The Telegraph for the report, noting the project faced repeated delays. Nscale stated it remains committed to the project and is exploring alternative power sources, while OpenAI also paused similar UK plans citing energy costs.
items.title: Microsoft Withdraws from UK Data Center Deal Due to Power Delays

items.summary: Adani Group Chairman Gautam Adani expressed interest in partnering with Shrimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur on grassroots projects. He visited the mission's headquarters in Gujarat with his wife, Dr Priti Adani, to seek blessings from founder Gurudevshri Rakeshji. Adani highlighted the importance of volunteer commitment over money for impactful service.
items.title: Adani Foundation Seeks Partnership with Shrimad Rajchandra Mission

items.summary: The Department of Justice charged 28 green card holders in California with election crimes, alleging illegal voter registration or voting. This action escalates tensions between the federal government and California regarding voting systems ahead of the midterm elections. Simultaneously, court records reveal that TikTok employees repeatedly raised concerns about child safety risks, including sexual exploitation and suicide content, which leadership allegedly ignored. The records also show the company avoided age surveys to prevent sharing data with the Federal Trade Commission. These findings highlight ongoing legal and safety challenges for both the DOJ and TikTok.
items.title: DOJ Charges 28 with Voting Crimes; TikTok Ignored Child Safety Warnings

items.summary: Andy describes the new Tesla Roadster as a feat of engineering but a defeat in the consumer market, noting it cannot outcompete Chinese rivals like BYD. The article argues that China's industrial strategy aims for national power rather than profit, creating a systemic challenge for Western automakers. Elon Musk warns that without trade barriers, China could demolish most global car companies. While Tesla's Shanghai gigafactory catalyzed the Chinese EV industry, Musk now bets on Tesla becoming a robot maker. Experts like Lu Feng and Kyle Chan highlight the clash between China's 'industrial socialism' and US 'financial capitalism,' suggesting Western firms must climb to rarefied niches or face destruction.
items.title: Tesla Roadster Represents Engineering Feat and Strategic Defeat Amid China Competition

items.summary: Britain's Competition and Markets Authority is consulting on proposals to lower fees and remove technical barriers for Apple's contactless payment technology. The regulator argues these measures will foster competition and innovation in the UK fintech sector. While noting that contactless payments now account for 39 per cent of all transactions, Apple has stated it does not believe the CMA should require lower privacy and security protections.
items.title: UK Regulator Proposes Rules to Loosen Apple's Payment Control

items.summary: Mukesh Ambani is launching Jio Platforms' IPO, aiming to raise up to 302bn rupees with a valuation of 10.3tn rupees. Despite a stock market downturn, the company secured 212 anchor investors. Shares will be offered to retail investors starting Wednesday, closing Friday. The valuation is lower than initial expectations of £110bn.
items.title: Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms launches India's largest IPO amid market slowdown

items.summary: Cognizant has expanded its partnership with Google Cloud to launch a new Gemini Frontier Capability Group, supported by approximately 18,000 associates. This dedicated workforce will leverage Google's AI platform to build and deploy production-grade autonomous agents for enterprise clients. The initiative focuses on legacy modernization and cyber defense, while Cognizant simultaneously scales internal Gemini adoption to 100,000 associates this year.
items.title: Cognizant Expands Partnership With Google Cloud For Agentic AI

items.summary: Amazon announced plans to invest over €16 billion in Germany by 2027 to expand cloud computing, AI, satellite internet, and media businesses. The company stated this investment aims to grow European operations amid surging AI demand. The package includes €4.8 billion for AWS Frankfurt expansion and projects expected to create over 3,000 jobs.
items.title: Amazon Plans €16 Billion Investment in Germany for 2027

items.summary: ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent have placed orders totaling over $35 billion for more than 3 million Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 graphics cards, according to two anonymous sources. These chips, priced at approximately $11,400 each, are export-compliant alternatives to restricted high-end models. Nvidia has warned it cannot guarantee full delivery due to high demand and production limits, with global output capped at 3 million units in 2027. The orders highlight continued Chinese appetite for Nvidia hardware despite US trade curbs, as companies seek AI computing capacity. Tansun Technology also reported purchasing 20,000 units, though delivery delays are possible.
items.title: Chinese Tech Giants Order $35 Billion in Nvidia Chips Amid Restrictions

items.summary: Shares of Sona BLW Precision Forgings Ltd, Solar Industries, Aurobindo Pharma, Oracle Financial Services Software, and CG Power and Industrials emerged as top midcap performers in 2026. These stocks rank among the top gainers of the Nifty Midcap 100 index, which is down about 3% this year due to the US-Iran War, FIIs-led selloff, weak rupee, and high crude prices.
items.title: Sona BLW and peers lead midcap gains despite index pressure

items.summary: Historian Yuval Noah Harari warns that artificial intelligence may take control of financial and legal systems within the next 10 to 20 years. He states that AI could create structures so complex that humans may no longer understand how they work or how decisions affecting their lives are made. Harari suggests the biggest threat comes from intelligent systems gradually taking over institutions that govern society rather than robots attacking humans.
items.title: Yuval Noah Harari Warns AI Could Control Financial and Legal Systems

items.summary: A leaked draft of an AI safety bill proposed by Anthropic to lawmakers has intensified debate regarding federal regulation. While Anthropic views the framework as a safety measure, critics argue it pre-empts state laws and accepts excessive risk. Competitor OpenAI seized the opportunity to assert that policy decisions must remain with elected officials rather than a single company, emphasizing the technology's profound implications for society and national security.
items.title: Anthropic Leaked AI Bill Draft Sparks Industry Backlash and Debate

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, donated $75 million to Vanderbilt University to help establish a new college focused on art, architecture, and design at its planned San Francisco campus. Announced on July 21, 2026, the gift helped attract additional contributions, pushing total philanthropic support for the campus beyond $100 million, according to the university. The new Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College is intended to combine creative disciplines with technology, engineering, and entrepreneurship. The campus is expected to open in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, and will serve approximately 1,000 undergraduate and graduate students. The initiative reflects the family's belief that artistic creativity is important to technological progress and business innovation.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and wife donate $75 million to Vanderbilt

items.summary: Data centres are increasingly viewed as critical targets in modern conflicts, as demonstrated by recent attacks in Russia and the Middle East. Ukrainian drones struck three Yandex facilities in October, disrupting services like email and payments, while Iranian drones damaged Amazon Web Services infrastructure in the UAE and Bahrain in March 2026. These incidents highlight the vulnerability of fixed digital infrastructure essential for artificial intelligence and essential services. Experts note that unlike mobile equipment, data centres require stable power and cooling, making them difficult to relocate. The attacks underscore the need for robust recovery plans and diversified backup systems to maintain operations during armed conflict.
items.title: Data Centres Emerge as Strategic Targets in Modern Warfare

items.summary: Apple India's revenue from operations reached Rs. 1,03,853 crore in FY2026, marking the first time it crossed the Rs. 1 lakh crore milestone. Net profit rose 66 percent to Rs. 5,311 crore. This growth was driven by resilient iPhone demand in the premium segment, contrasting with a decline in Samsung's mobile phone revenue. Industry estimates suggest iPhone shipments rose about 24 percent year-on-year.
items.title: Apple India Revenue Crosses ₹1 Lakh Crore Mark

items.summary: A study in Addis Ababa finds that subsidizing formal vacancy advertising causes firms to shift demand toward white-collar positions they struggle to fill. While the intervention increased formal advertising, the share of filled vacancies dropped significantly, particularly for white-collar roles. Researchers attribute this to a mismatch between firm expectations and applicant wage demands, suggesting inexperienced firms may have set unrealistic hiring goals. Despite immediate hiring difficulties, firms reportedly learned from the experience and reverted to informal search, potentially improving future hiring decisions.
items.title: Subsidized Job Ads in Ethiopia Shift Demand to Hard-to-Fill White-Collar Roles

items.summary: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt holds a stake in Anthropic from a 2021 Series A round. While the company is preparing for an IPO, investors disagree on its valuation, with estimates ranging from $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion. Schmidt's representatives declined to comment on the potential value of his shares.
items.title: Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt's Anthropic Stake Valuation Uncertain Ahead of IPO

items.summary: 3M reported adjusted earnings of $2.50 a share, a 12% rise, driven by a new non-GAAP treatment of amortization. Adjusted sales reached $6.6 billion. The company issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary for up to 3,162,015 shares, with 85% vesting upon reaching $6 billion in spending. CEO William Brown cited strong results and robust free cash flow.
items.title: 3M Reports Strong Earnings and Announces Amazon Partnership

items.summary: Singapore plans to accredit its first five traditional Chinese medicine providers as part of a broader push to integrate TCM into mainstream care under Healthier SG. Porsche Poh of Silver Ribbon (Singapore) supports this move, citing client autonomy and the need for shared decision-making. The initiative aims to create a more inclusive, person-centred healthcare approach that respects patient choices while maintaining evidence-based standards.
items.title: Singapore moves to accredit TCM providers for inclusive healthcare

items.summary: Konstantin Levinzon of Planet VPN warns that the EU KIDS Act proposal could compromise young gamers' privacy. While the European Commission aims to strengthen protections for children on digital platforms, Levinzon argues that age verification methods may require processing sensitive identity documents or facial images. He cites a 2025 Discord security incident where approximately 70,000 users' government ID photographs were exposed by a third-party provider. Levinzon contends that collecting such biometric data creates significant risks if systems are compromised, urging regulators and developers to adopt privacy-preserving verification approaches that minimize data collection and ensure secure handling by third parties.
items.title: EU KIDS Act Privacy Risks for Young Gamers

items.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar held talks in Mumbai to finalize a trade deal. While officials stated negotiations are nearly complete, some items remain to be wrapped up. The discussions aim to deepen energy cooperation and resolve stalled negotiations over tariffs and Russian oil purchases. Both nations seek to revive trade talks despite ongoing tensions.
items.title: Rubio and Jaishankar Finalize Trade Deal Details in Mumbai

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Mumbai to discuss trade and energy cooperation with India. He highlighted the growing partnership and noted that trade negotiations are nearing completion. The visit includes an inspection of Reliance Industries' Jamnagar refinery, which plays a key role in processing crude oil amid US energy shortages and global supply disruptions.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio Visits India for Trade and Energy Talks

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on Tuesday that the proposed India-US trade agreement is nearing finalisation, with only a few issues remaining. Speaking in Mumbai, he expressed optimism that the two countries could soon announce progress on the long-pending pact. Rubio noted they are very close to execution, though the deal has not yet been formally signed. The remarks come as both nations seek to advance negotiations despite differences over tariffs and energy security.
items.title: Marco Rubio Says India-US Trade Deal Nears Finalisation Ahead Of Meeting With Jaishankar

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Mumbai for high-level discussions with External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, emphasizing growing commercial and defense partnerships. While addressing trade negotiations, Rubio noted that only a small number of items remain to be finalized. The visit also included energy security cooperation, with plans to inspect Reliance Industries' oil refinery in Jamnagar. Concurrently, Union Home Minister Amit Shah visited Punjab to meet families of anti-drug activists who died, highlighting ongoing political tensions between major parties ahead of assembly elections.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio Visits India for Trade and Defense Talks Amid Regional Tensions

items.summary: Apple India Pvt Ltd reported a 31% year-on-year rise in revenue from operations to ₹1,03,853 crore for the year ended March 2026, according to filings accessed via AltInfo. This growth significantly outpaced the 18% recorded in the previous fiscal year, driven by a narrowing price gap between iPhones and Android flagships. Counterpoint Technology Market Research noted India's overall smartphone market grew 2% by volume and 9% by value in FY26, with the premium segment expanding at 12%.
items.title: Apple India Revenue Surges 31% in FY26 Amid Market Growth

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India to discuss trade and strategic relations with Foreign Minister Jaishankar. Rubio stated that a trade agreement is nearly finalized and expected to be signed shortly. He highlighted India's role as a refining superpower and potential cooperation regarding Venezuelan oil. Rubio also addressed the Ukraine war and proposed arms control talks involving China, Russia, and the US.
items.title: Rubio Arrives in India to Discuss Trade and Strategic Relations

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio began a three-day visit to India, focusing on trade, energy, and defense amid ongoing bilateral friction. He is expected to meet External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar to discuss strengthening the India-US partnership.
